title: Circuit-level benchmarks of GKP-concatenated qLDPC Codes
authors: Yuan Yao, Ruipeng Xing, Jianshuo Gao, Xiao Yuan
abstract: Scalable fault-tolerant quantum error correction based on Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes requires finite-rate outer codes that can exploit analog GKP information under realistic circuit noise. However, quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) outer codes have not been systematically compared as candidates for circuit-level GKP concatenation. Here, we benchmark BB and tricycle codes using a unified simulation framework that progresses from code-capacity noise to repeated noisy syndrome extraction and schedule-resolved displacement propagation. Across all three noise models, analog-informed belief-propagation with ordered-statistics decoding (BP-OSD) yields higher finite-size crossing estimates than hard-decision decoding. In the full circuit model, the analog-informed crossings are \(σ_{\mathrm{th}}\simeq0.212\) for the selected BB sequence and \(0.142\) for the tricycle sequence, corresponding to squeezing requirements of approximately \(10.46\,\mathrm{dB}\) and \(13.94\,\mathrm{dB}\), respectively. These results show that analog GKP information continues to improve decoding under circuit-level noise. Under the common simulation assumptions used here, the selected BB sequence also yields a higher finite-size crossing estimate than the selected tricycle sequence.
summary: This paper benchmarks the performance of GKP-concatenated quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes (BB and tricycle) for fault-tolerant quantum computation. By simulating error propagation through a detailed circuit model, the authors demonstrate that incorporating analog GKP information into the decoding process significantly improves error thresholds compared to traditional hard-decision methods. The results guide the selection of optimal outer codes for practical quantum hardware.
main_problem: Developing scalable fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) using GKP-concatenated outer codes, specifically comparing the performance of BB and tricycle qLDPC codes.
main_result: Analog-informed belief-propagation decoding consistently outperforms hard-decision decoding across all noise models, and the BB sequence yields a higher finite-size crossing estimate than the tricycle sequence in the full circuit model.
method: The authors developed a unified simulation framework to benchmark GKP-concatenated codes across three noise models, comparing decoding strategies (hard vs. analog-informed BP-OSD).
model_or_system: The system involves encoding logical qubits using Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes, which are then concatenated with outer qLDPC codes (BB and tricycle). The process simulates error propagation through syndrome extraction using bosonic interactions.
key_observables: Finite-size crossing estimates ($\sigma_{th}$), squeezing requirements (e.g., 10.46 dB for BB), and word logical error rates.
important_parameters: Noise strength ($\sigma$), code parameters (BB/tricycle structure), and the choice of decoder (hard vs. analog-informed).
main_assumptions: The reported values are finite-length benchmarks for specific code instances, and the analysis assumes that the benefit of analog GKP information persists under circuit-level noise.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the processing stack for GKP-concatenated QEC, showing the inner GKP correction and outer-code stabilizer extraction. Figure 4 compares word logical error rates for GKP–BB and GKP–tricycle concatenation under different noise assumptions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes a unified simulation framework, details the error modeling (hard vs. analog-informed), benchmarks the BB and tricycle codes across increasing levels of circuit noise (from code-capacity to schedule-resolved propagation), and compares decoding performance metrics.
why_interesting: The work provides concrete, circuit-level benchmarks for advanced QEC schemes, directly relevant to hardware implementation efforts in quantum computing.

(b) Each physical qubit of the outer code is replaced by a bosonic mode encoding a GKP qubit. (c) Inner Steane-type GKP correction uses ancillary GKP states, Gaussian interactions, homodyne measurements, and classical feedback to estimate and suppress displacement errors. The crossing estimates are (0.369, 0.329) for analog and hard BB decoding and (0.349, 0.334) for analog and hard tricycle decoding, respectively.
